info.name: EDI Middleware — Let's Try Foods (Full API)
info.description:
Complete API collection for the EDI Middleware (SAP Business One integration).

═══ SETUP (2 minutes) ═══

1. Collection → Variables tab. Set:
     baseUrl        http://localhost:8001                      (local Docker api)
                    https://www.letstryfoods.com/edi-backend   (server)
     email          your login email
     password       your login password
     webhookApiKey  BLINKIT webhook secret — only needed for folder 15

   Get the webhook secret with:
     SELECT webhook_secret FROM trading_partners WHERE code='BLINKIT';

2. Run "00 · Health" — confirms baseUrl is right before you debug anything else.
3. Run "01 · Auth → Login" — stores {{token}}; every other request then just works.

═══ TWO KINDS OF AUTH ═══

  Folders 01-14   Authorization: Bearer {{token}}   (run Login first)
  Folder 15       api-key: {{webhookApiKey}}        (no login — this is how partners call us)

Mixing these up is the single most common mistake. A webhook partner has no user
account, so a Bearer token is not an option for them.

═══ ID CHAINING ═══

List requests capture ids into variables automatically, so run them before the
requests that use them:

  List POs            → {{poId}}, {{poNumber}}
  Get PO detail       → {{buyerSku}}
  List invoices       → {{invoiceId}}
  List customers      → {{partnerId}}
  List items          → {{materialId}}
  List ship-to        → {{shipToId}}
  List bill-to        → {{billToId}}
  List messages       → {{messageId}}
  List exceptions     → {{issueId}}
  List B1 logs        → {{b1LogId}}

Check the Postman Console (View → Show Postman Console) for what each one captured.

═══ THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU ═══

• /auth/login has NO /api prefix. Every other route does.
• The api container publishes on 8001, not 8000.
• Disabled query params are filters — tick them on to use them.
• Invoice push: ALWAYS read results[]. An invoice can be stored yet HELD, with
  asn_dispatched=false and the reason in issues[]. The counters alone will mislead you.
• Sync order matters: Items BEFORE SKU mappings; Customers BEFORE anything partner-scoped.
• Anything you POST creates real rows. Point baseUrl at localhost while testing.

Dummy data uses the fictional customer DEMOMART so it cannot collide with live partners.

item.description: SAP pushes A/R Invoices here; receiving one raises and dispatches its ASN.

request.description:
Idempotent on invoice_number — re-pushing updates (typically to add the IRN) and never raises a second ASN.

{{poNumber}} and {{buyerSku}} are filled by 'List POs' and 'Get PO detail'. Run those first, or hardcode real values.

ALWAYS read results[] — an invoice can be stored but HELD (asn_dispatched=false) with the reason in issues[].

item.name: 15 · Webhooks (partner → us)
item.description: Authenticates with the api-key header ONLY. No login, no Bearer token.

request.description:
This is exactly what Blinkit's server sends — a webhook IS just a POST.

Partner code in the path must be uppercase and match trading_partners.code.
  wrong key   → 401
  unknown code → 404

The response body IS the acknowledgement: Blinkit reads data.po_status.

exec: console.log('404 → partner code in the URL does not exist.');

request.description: Proves auth is enforced. This is the exact failure Blinkit reports when their key is wrong.
Confirms routing: an unrecognised partner code 404s before any auth check.
